rationale: Refined the last open repair-path limit from "not exercised" to a reasoned negative. The divergent entries sit at the highest index in every log at the time they are committed, and a later leader can only be elected with a log at least as up-to-date as its voters (requestVote rejects a candidate whose last term is lower, or whose last index is smaller at the same term), so no later leader can write a different entry at that same index: it can only append beyond it, where the duplicate-skip leaves the difference untouched. Truncation by a different term would need a leader whose log is shorter at that index, which the vote rule excludes in this scenario. I acquired that vote rule as a source and recorded it, then updated the repair-path interpretation and the child account so the remaining limit is the argument rather than an untested path.

knowledge.statement: A candidate is granted votes only if its log is at least as up to date as the voter's: requestVote rejects a candidate whose last log term is lower, or whose last log index is smaller at the same term. Consequently, once an entry at an index has been committed in term T by a leader whose log was the most up to date, any later leader must have a log whose last entry is at least as up to date, so it can only append entries beyond that index and cannot replace the entry at it with a different term; the entry can only be replaced by a snapshot install or a user restore.
knowledge.conditions: Voter-side vote admission (raft.go 1725-1750) applied to the split-brain state of this defect, where the conflicting entries are at the highest index of every log and at the same term.

interpretations.rationale: Answer: the divergence left by this defect is reconciled by replacing the node's state, not by ordinary log comparison, and only two of the three candidate mechanisms actually apply. A node that falls behind a compacted leader is sent a snapshot and ends up with the leader's FSM state, entry suffix and configuration (receipt 112186e8b9544b51b4f7818a04c78a84), repairing that node only. A leader-side restore converges the cluster (receipt 6ff0ef691a0141449142bfa06719bb47, where all five applied write lists agree and the minority write is gone). Truncation by a different term does not arise: the conflicting entries are at the highest index of every log at the same term, and vote admission requires a candidate's log to be at least as up to date as the voter's (raft.go 1725-1750), so a later leader can only append beyond that index, where same-term duplicates are skipped (raft.go 1526-1553); the long-run and configuration-change receipts show the difference surviving exactly that. Remaining limits: the per-node repair needed harness-arranged lag and the restore used a snapshot the leader produced itself; the samples are single per mode with in-memory stores and scaled timeouts.
counterevidence: Without either replacement mechanism the long-run and configuration-change receipts show the divergence persisting, so neither path is engaged by ordinary operation while the node keeps up.
The per-node repair leaves an up-to-date divergent node untouched, whereas the restore converges the cluster, so the two mechanisms are not interchangeable.
limitations: The per-node repair needed harness-arranged lag and the cluster-wide repair used a snapshot the leader produced itself.
Single samples per mode with in-memory stores and scaled timeouts.
The term-truncation route is argued unavailable from the vote rule rather than tested; a variant of the defect that left a shorter log on a node able to win votes could change that.
interpretations.joint_history: Four receipts of four fixed experiments over the same divergent state: fa1f90c2eefd45e6af45d7593ac53205 (cited through its successors) records the healed divergence, 112186e8b9544b51b4f7818a04c78a84 the per-node snapshot install, 6ff0ef691a0141449142bfa06719bb47 the leader-side restore, and the long-run and configuration-change receipts (861a2b3c62bb44d7aed2eee9b95aa15f, 182740a6d29f4af9a99cf83c49f2e857) show that neither the entry nor the applied state is reconciled while the node keeps up. All observe the same cluster identity, conflict index and payloads, and each comparison outcome is read from its own receipt.

interpretations.rationale: Answer: yes, with both consequences bounded and the repair options identified. A node left with a stale configuration by the RestoreCommittedLogs replay wins an election with fewer votes than the configuration recorded in its own committed log while the other voters elect their own leader, both sides commit at the same index and term, and after healing the entry and applied divergence survives a long run and a configuration change; the stale membership itself ends at the next configuration change (receipt 182740a6d29f4af9a99cf83c49f2e857 index 4) and the divergence is removed either per node by a snapshot install or cluster-wide by a leader-side restore (receipt 6ff0ef691a0141449142bfa06719bb47 index 5). Ordinary log comparison does not reconcile it: the conflicting entries share the highest index and the same term, and vote admission requires a candidate's log to be at least as up to date as the voter's, so a later leader can only append beyond that index. Remaining limits: the configuration change was a single harness-issued AddVoter; the long run is entry-count based; the per-node repair needed harness-arranged lag and the restore used a self-produced snapshot; and in-memory stores with scaled timeouts were used.
counterevidence: The feature-off control run over the identical scenario, long run, configuration change and restore shows no stale membership, no minority leader and no self-applied write.
A later configuration entry ends the stale membership, and both replacement paths remove the divergent entry and applied state.
Without a replacement the earlier receipts show the divergence persisting while the node keeps up, so the consequences are bounded by repair timing rather than by ordinary operation.
limitations: The configuration change is a single harness-issued AddVoter and the long run is ~200 entries without a snapshot install.
The per-node repair needed harness-arranged lag and the cluster-wide repair used a snapshot the leader produced itself.
Ordinary log comparison is argued unable to reconcile the divergence from the vote rule rather than tested.
In-memory stores, scaled timeouts and a graceful shutdown rather than a crash.
interpretations.joint_history: Nine receipts of eight fixed experiments over one defect chain, sharing the structural fixture (snapshot configuration {A,B,C}, a committed configuration entry with {A,B,C,D,E} above it, a persisted commit index covering it) and the feature-on restart reporting {A,B,C} against the control reporting {A,B,C,D,E}. They successively construct the restart state, observe the split, add healing, applied-state sampling, the per-node repair phase, the feature-off control, a long run, a configuration change and the leader-side restore. The three receipts cited here are the newest members of that chain (long run 861a2b3c62bb44d7aed2eee9b95aa15f, configuration change 182740a6d29f4af9a99cf83c49f2e857, leader-side restore 6ff0ef691a0141449142bfa06719bb47); each comparison outcome is read from its own receipt and no value is combined across them.
